identity_evidence.quote: We report the case of a 76-year-old patient who underwent evacuation of a posterior fossa hematoma.

attribution_limitations: Postoperative-day numbering uses different, unstated reference surgeries: day 19 follows the index craniectomy, whereas days 6, 8 and 12 are not explicitly anchored (the abstract says death 12 days after surgical revision).
The abstract names a surgical revision and the case text a wound debridement and skin closure; the source does not state that they are the same operation.
It is not stated whether "On admission" refers to the index admission or the readmission.
Table 1 (antibiogram) exists only as an image; its cells are not quotable source text, so no per-antibiotic facts are extracted. Carbapenemase type is only "likely KPC".
Susceptibility to meropenem-vaborbactam or cefiderocol is described as likely, not tested; these drugs were not given.
Authors hedge the nosocomial origin ("likely", "suggests") and attribute thromboembolic risk factors by interpretation, not as separately documented findings.

Culture results arrived five days after surgery, yet improvement 48 h after the treatment change is placed on postoperative day 6, which would put the change before the reported culture results; the narrative implies the change followed the results.
